key_insight: Spatially patterned spin rotations control the imaginary-time Mpemba effect by redistributing spectral weight away from slow-decaying modes without changing initial bipartite entanglement spectra or correlation magnitudes.
engineering_relevance: Twist-based initial-state design offers a controllable route to faster convergence in quantum ground-state preparation.
method: Apply spatially modulated local rotations to select higher-energy modes.
Use compact-boson theory to derive exact relaxation-crossing times.
Reintroduce slow-mode weight to systematically delay the effect.
evidence_signal: The mechanism is supported by interacting XXZ-chain and ladder calculations and a 12-qubit variational imaginary-time simulation reproducing relaxation reversals and controlled delays.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulations rather than hardware experiments, leaving robustness to device noise and variational errors unresolved.
paper_title: Twist-controlled imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems
